newsitem.title: GERMANY: Delta drops cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Delta drops cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: Delta Air Lines said it will drop its 10 US cents per kg cargo fuel surcharge with immediate effect.

Danita Waterfall, Delta Air Lines regional director cargo sales Europe, said: "We have continually monitored the fuel situation and over the past few weeks have seen a significant decrease in fuel prices.
"Although fuel prices have not reached last year's levels, Delta Air Lines will discontinue the fuel surcharge effective immediately," she said in a circular to agents made available to Reuters.
Delta imposed a 10 cents per kg surcharge on all freight shipments between the US and Europe/Asia on November 8, 1996, the letter added.

A cargo fuel surcharge of 15 pfennigs per kg, then roughly equivalent to 10 cents, was first introduced by Lufthansa Cargo AG on November 1 at just three days notice and rapidly followed by airlines in most world markets.
A similar surcharge was later added to passenger fares by most airlines in the International Air Transport Association(IATA).
But the measure prompted an angry response from forwarders and, in particular, from air cargo shippers who protested at the lack of notice given before the hike.
Dutch and French forwarders spoke out strongly against the measure while German colleagues were more cautious in their reaction.
